title: Mirabai Chanu Completes Historic Hat-Trick of Commonwealth Games Gold With Record-Breaking Performance in Glasgow
excerpt: The Olympic silver medallist lifted a CWG-record 190 kg to win the women's 48 kg title, becoming a three-time Commonwealth champion and delivering India's first gold of Glasgow 2026.
body:
• Mirabai Chanu won gold in the women's 48 kg weightlifting at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, completing a hat-trick of CWG titles
  • She lifted a total of 190 kg (85 kg snatch, 105 kg clean and jerk), setting three new Commonwealth Games records in the process
  • Nigeria's Ruth Nyong took silver (168 kg) and Malaysia's Irene Jane Henry won bronze (167 kg)
  • The gold is India's first of the Glasgow 2026 Games, adding to Chanu's Olympic silver from Tokyo 2021

Three Games, Three Golds

Mirabai Chanu made history on Sunday at the Scottish Event Campus in Glasgow, winning her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal in the women's 48 kg weightlifting event. The 31-year-old from Manipur dominated the competition with a combined lift of 190 kg, setting three new Commonwealth Games records and delivering India's first gold of Glasgow 2026.

The victory extends one of the most remarkable streaks in Commonwealth weightlifting. Chanu won gold at Gold Coast 2018, gold at Birmingham 2022, and has now capped the trilogy in Glasgow — all while competing at the highest levels of Olympic and World Championship competition in between.

"Her total of 190 kg set yet another Commonwealth Games record."

A Rocky Start, a Record Finish

The final did not begin smoothly. Chanu missed her opening snatch attempt at 82 kg, momentarily raising anxiety among Indian fans watching in the arena and around the world. But the composure that has defined her career kicked in. She successfully lifted 82 kg on her second attempt and then went for broke — clearing 85 kg on her third lift to set a new Commonwealth Games record and earning a standing ovation from the Glasgow crowd.

The clean and jerk followed a similar pattern. She missed her first attempt at 105 kg but nailed it on the second, and with the gold already secure, opted not to attempt a third lift. Her total of 190 kg set yet another Commonwealth Games record.

Nigeria's Ruth Nyong claimed silver with a total of 168 kg — a full 22 kg behind Chanu — while Malaysia's Irene Jane Henry took bronze with 167 kg. Sri Lanka's Upamalika Jambulliye Gamladdalage and Papua New Guinea's Thelma Toua both recorded no marks, failing to complete valid lifts.

From Manipur to the World Stage

Chanu's journey from the small town of Nongpok Kakching in Manipur to the pinnacle of global weightlifting is one of Indian sport's most compelling stories. Inspired by legendary Indian weightlifter Kunjarani Devi, she took up the sport as a teenager and developed under coach Vijay Sharma into one of the country's most decorated athletes.

Her career highlights read like a greatest-hits compilation: a silver medal at the 2016 World Championships, gold at the 2017 Worlds, an Olympic silver at Tokyo 2021, and another World Championship silver in October 2025. Earlier this year, she broke three national records at the Senior National Weightlifting Championships with lifts of 89 kg (snatch), 116 kg (clean and jerk) and a 205 kg total — numbers that would have shattered the CWG field.

The one prize that has eluded her is an Olympic gold. At Paris 2024, she narrowly missed the podium in the 49 kg category, finishing fourth with a 199 kg total — just 1 kg behind the bronze medallist. The weight class restructuring by the International Weightlifting Federation saw her shift to 48 kg for the Commonwealth circuit.

India's CWG Campaign Builds Momentum

Chanu's gold capped a productive Day 4 for India at Glasgow 2026. Rishikanta Singh had earlier claimed silver in the men's 60 kg weightlifting with a total of 264 kg, behind Malaysia's Aniq Kasdan. In boxing, Jadumani Singh defeated Pakistan's Sumama Rehman to advance to the men's 55 kg quarter-finals, while Preeti Pawar stormed into the women's 54 kg quarters after the referee stopped her bout against Malawi's Deborah Mtenje in the second round.

India's swimmers also made progress, with the men's 4x200m freestyle relay team qualifying for the final. With weightlifting, boxing and several other events still to unfold, India's medal tally is expected to grow significantly over the remaining days in Glasgow.
